findings.title: Heat loss at Door #1
findings.description: Heat loss detected at door visible in 7 images. Temperature readings range from 20.0°C to 20.0°C, averaging 20.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Install or replace door sweep at bottom to prevent air infiltration
Add weather stripping to frame perimeter for better seal
Consider installing a thermal door curtain for additional insulation
Check threshold and seal any gaps with appropriate materials
Ensure door closer is adjusted for proper seal when closed
recommendations.description: External doors are common heat loss points, particularly around frames and thresholds. Poor sealing can result in significant air leakage.

findings.title: Heat loss at Wall #2
findings.description: Heat loss detected at wall visible in 2 images. Temperature readings range from 20.0°C to 20.0°C, averaging 20.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Inspect cavity wall insulation levels and top up if necessary
Consider external wall insulation (EWI) for solid wall properties
Investigate internal wall insulation (IWI) as alternative to EWI
Check for thermal bridging at structural elements (lintels, columns)
Investigate any signs of damp or missing insulation in cavity
Consider thermal render or insulated plasterboard solutions
recommendations.description: Wall heat loss is one of the largest contributors to energy waste in buildings. Solid walls lose heat twice as fast as cavity walls, and poorly insulated cavity walls are also highly inefficient.

findings.title: Heat loss at Eaves #3
findings.description: Heat loss detected at eaves location. Temperature readings range from 20.0°C to 20.0°C, averaging 20.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Improve loft insulation to recommended 270mm depth (glass wool) or 250mm (mineral wool)
Seal gaps between wall and roof structure to prevent air leakage
Check ventilation/insulation balance to prevent condensation issues
Install eaves insulation baffles to maintain airflow while improving insulation
Ensure insulation extends right to eaves but doesn't block soffit vents
Consider spray foam or rigid board insulation for difficult eaves areas
recommendations.description: Heat rises, making the eaves area a critical heat loss point. Inadequate insulation at the eaves can undermine the entire roof insulation system.

findings.title: Heat loss at Vent #4
findings.description: Heat loss detected at vent location. Temperature readings range from 20.0°C to 20.0°C, averaging 20.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Install controllable trickle vents to balance ventilation with heat retention
Assess whether vent is necessary or can be sealed (check building regulations)
Consider mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR) system
Ensure existing vents serve their intended purpose and aren't over-ventilating
Install vent covers that can be closed when not needed
Check for uncontrolled air leakage around vent installations
recommendations.description: While ventilation is essential for air quality and preventing condensation, uncontrolled ventilation leads to unnecessary heat loss. Modern controlled ventilation systems can dramatically reduce this issue.
